disclaimer.subtitle: ADOS Mission Control은 실제 항공기를 제어할 수 있습니다. 아래 내용을 읽고 동의해 주세요.

lawfulUse.heading: 합법적 사용만 가능
lawfulUse.body: 본 소프트웨어를 합법적인 목적으로만 사용하는 데 동의합니다. 감시, 개인 괴롭힘, 사생활 침해 또는 해당 국가나 지역의 법률로 금지된 활동을 지원하기 위해 사용하지 않습니다.

militaryUse.heading: 무단 군사 사용 금지
militaryUse.body: 본 소프트웨어는 관련 정부 당국의 명시적 승인 없이 공격적 군사 또는 국방 작전에 사용해서는 안 됩니다. 무인항공기의 무단 무기화는 거의 모든 관할권에서 불법입니다.

aviationRegs.heading: 항공 규정
aviationRegs.body: 귀하의 위치와 운용에 적용되는 모든 항공 규정을 준수할 책임은 전적으로 귀하에게 있습니다. 이에는 다음이 포함되지만 이에 국한되지 않습니다:
aviationRegs.item1: 해당 기관(DGCA, FAA, CASA, EASA 등)에 드론 등록

aviationRegs.item4: 고도, 거리 및 가시거리 제한 내 운용
aviationRegs.footer: 본 소프트웨어는 규정 준수를 보장하지 않습니다. 이것은 도구입니다. 귀하가 기장입니다.

exportControls.heading: 수출 통제
exportControls.body: 드론 제어 소프트웨어는 ITAR(미국), EAR(미국), EU 이중사용 규정 및 인도 SCOMET 목록을 포함한 수출 통제법의 적용을 받을 수 있습니다. 본 소프트웨어의 사용, 배포 또는 수정이 해당 수출 통제 및 제재법을 준수하는지 확인할 책임은 귀하에게 있습니다.

noWarranty.heading: 무보증 및 위험 감수
noWarranty.warranty: 본 소프트웨어는 명시적이든 묵시적이든 어떠한 종류의 보증 없이 "있는 그대로" 제공됩니다. 여기에는 상품성, 특정 목적 적합성 및 비침해에 대한 보증이 포함되지만 이에 국한되지 않습니다.
noWarranty.risk: 드론은 부적절한 조작이나 소프트웨어 오작동 시 재산 피해, 부상 또는 사망을 초래할 수 있는 물리적 기계입니다. 본 소프트웨어를 사용함으로써 그 사용과 관련된 모든 위험을 감수합니다. Altnautica와 기여자들은 직접적, 간접적, 부수적 또는 결과적 여부에 관계없이 본 소프트웨어 사용으로 인한 어떠한 청구, 손해 또는 손실에 대해서도 책임을 지지 않습니다.

swarm.title: Swarm
swarm.blurb: Multi-drone coordination configuration stored on this node's agent.
swarm.slotHint: Issued by the ground station at pair time. Formation offsets are indexed by it, so it is reported here and edited nowhere.
swarm.enabledHint: Master switch for the node's swarm services.
swarm.formationHint: The formation preset the node starts with.

swarm.cohesionHint: Pull toward the local group's centre, as a percentage of unit gain (40 means 0.40).

swarm.separationGainHint: Strength of the push away from a close neighbour, as a percentage of unit gain (150 means 1.50).
swarm.flockRadiusHint: Neighbours beyond this range contribute nothing to cohesion or alignment.
swarm.flockNeighborsHint: How many of the nearest neighbours inside the radius are weighted, so a dense cluster cannot dominate the solution.
swarm.sepRadiusHint: Below this distance the drone pushes away from a neighbour. Must stay above the hard floor.
swarm.sepHardHint: Below this distance the horizontal solution is abandoned for a hold and a slot-indexed climb, overriding every other mode.
swarm.separationConfirmMessage: Separation is the collision-avoidance layer, not a preference. A larger value makes the fleet spread; a smaller one lets aircraft close on each other before anything intervenes. Apply this change?
swarm.precedenceHint: Highest authority first. A drone whose separation layer has taken over is in hard separation whatever mode was commanded.
swarm.precedenceHardSeparation: Hard separation — a neighbour inside the hard floor

macPin.candidateHint: This adapter looks like it randomizes its MAC. Confirm the pin on the node with

selfHeal.title: Self-heal
selfHeal.blurb: Always-on protections that repair the node's own connectivity and camera without operator action.
selfHeal.wifiSelfHealHint: Re-associates the onboard management Wi-Fi when it is connected but passing no traffic. Only ever touches onboard managed Wi-Fi, never the radio adapter or a wired link.
selfHeal.cameraRecoveryHint: Recovers an expected camera that failed to enumerate by re-binding the device or power-cycling its port. Steps that could disturb other devices stay gated.
selfHeal.guardianHint: Watches the operator's path to the node and climbs an escalating repair ladder when the link dies. Always on; tunable only in the node's configuration file.
selfHeal.reconcilerHint: Holds the global regulatory domain to the configured value so a radio adapter's baked-in country can never kill the onboard network. Recent re-pins appear in the activity feed.
selfHeal.eventsUnavailable: Event history needs the node's on-device log store, reachable over the LAN.

mavlinkRouting.blurb: How this node connects to the flight controller, exposes MAVLink endpoints, and forwards telemetry.
mavlinkRouting.transportHint: Managed from the node's Overview tab (FC connection picker), which validates the change against a live heartbeat.
mavlinkRouting.endpointsNotReported: The node's configuration does not carry an endpoint list.
mavlinkRouting.systemIdHint: The MAVLink system ID this node's router speaks with (1-255).
mavlinkRouting.componentIdHint: The MAVLink component ID this node's router speaks with (2-255). 1 is the autopilot's own ID and 0 is broadcast, so neither is accepted.
mavlinkRouting.signingRequiresLan: Signing status needs a LAN connection to the node.
mavlinkRouting.signingUnexposed: Not exposed by this agent version.

security.title: Security
security.blurb: The node's access posture: pairing key state, connection enforcement, and the dashboard PIN.
security.apiKeyHint: Issued when the node is paired; the value is never shown here. To issue a new key, unpair the node and pair it again — in-place rotation is not exposed by the agent.
security.wsEnforceHint: When on, a paired node rejects off-box raw-MAVLink WebSocket connections that present no valid pairing key. On-box and unpaired connections stay open. When off, an unauthorized connection is logged but still admitted.
security.setupTokenHint: When on, every setup mutation needs the token generated on the node at first boot. When off, any browser served the setup pages from the node's own port is trusted.
security.pinHint: Gates the node's own web dashboard when opened from another device. Set or reset it from this node's Health tab, on the Dashboard access card.
security.pinNoPath: The PIN posture can only be read through a stored pairing record for this node. Manage the PIN on the node's own dashboard, or from the Health tab once the node is paired over the LAN.
security.missionControlUrlHint: The Mission Control address this node advertises in its setup flow. Blank offers only a localhost link.
security.restBindHint: The address and port the node's HTTP API listens on. Set at install; changing it needs a reinstall.
security.wsEnforceConfirmMessage: With enforcement off, a paired node admits off-box raw-MAVLink WebSocket connections that present no pairing key, so an unauthenticated caller on the network could send commands straight to the flight controller. Only turn this off on a trusted, isolated link.
security.setupTokenConfirmMessage: With the token no longer required, any browser that can reach the node's setup pages is trusted to change its configuration. Only turn this off on a trusted network.

radio.title: Radio
radio.blurb: Fleet addressing, the WFB link switches and the modulation rung for this node's radio.
radio.notAdvertised: This agent's config surface does not expose a WFB radio block, so there is nothing to configure here.
radio.fleetIdHint: Every node that must hear every other node shares this. Two fleets can share one channel without hearing each other.
radio.fleetSlotHint: Issued by the ground station when this node pairs. Two nodes on one slot re-initialise each other's decoder about once a second, which reads as unexplained link loss — so the slot is never hand-edited here.
radio.presetHint: The MCS + FEC combination the radio starts with. Conservative keeps any explicitly set per-key values.
radio.bandHint: The channel whitelist automatic hopping scans.
radio.autoHopHint: Moves the link to the quietest channel in the band, coordinated with the radio peer.
radio.adaptiveHint: Steps bitrate and FEC down as the link degrades and back up as it recovers.
radio.mcsHint: The modulation rung the transmitter starts on. Each step up buys throughput and costs link margin.
radio.mcsLiveHint: The rung the transmitter is actually running, read back from the link — not the value stored above.
radio.mcsAutoHint: The adaptive ladder owns the rung while adaptive bitrate is on. Turn adaptive off to set one by hand.
radio.channelHint: The rendezvous channel. Pairing and automatic hopping manage it.
radio.txPowerHint: Managed live from the Link tab's power slider.
radio.mcsCapHint: The highest rung the ladder may climb to. Defaults to 3; anything above it is bench-only until the driver sweep says the rung holds at range. A ceiling of 1 pins the ladder to the floor.
radio.fleetIdConfirmMessage: A node hears only nodes with the same fleet ID. After its next radio start this node cannot hear any peer on a different fleet ID, including its ground station, so every node in the fleet must be changed to match.
radio.mcsPresetHint: The link preset sets the rung at every radio start and replaces a stored value. Switch the preset to Conservative to set the rung by hand.

display.title: Display
display.rendererBlurb: Which renderer this ground station brings up at boot. The display service gates its startup on this, and the on-box display is how you recover a node whose network is down, so only renderers the node reports as attached can be selected.
display.kioskBlurb: The full-screen browser the HDMI output runs. Applies when the renderer resolves to HDMI.
display.kioskTargetUrlHint: The page the kiosk opens. Leave empty to use this node's own console.
display.kioskAlwaysOn: The kiosk runs whenever the renderer above resolves to HDMI and a display is attached. To take it off the screen, choose a different renderer.

battery.title: Battery setup
battery.blurb: The limits the node's battery engine checks every flight-controller battery report against. A crossing raises an anomaly on the Live view, in the node's event log, and as an alert here.
battery.orderNote: Critical cell must stay below Low cell. The node rejects a pair that crosses and keeps the previous values.
battery.enabledHint: Evaluate the cell, sag, temperature and time-to-reserve rules on the node. The flight controller's own battery failsafes are not affected either way.
battery.lowCellMvHint: A cell below this raises a warning. 2500 to 4200 mV, above Critical cell.
battery.criticalCellMvHint: A cell below this raises a critical alert. 2500 to 4000 mV, below Low cell.
battery.cellDivergenceMvHint: Spread between the highest and lowest cell that raises a warning. 10 to 500 mV.
battery.voltageDropMvPerSHint: Pack voltage falling faster than this raises a warning. 100 to 5000 mV per second.
battery.tempSpikeDcPerSHint: Pack temperature rising faster than this raises a warning, in tenths of a degree per second (50 is 5 °C/s). 5 to 200.
battery.predictiveWindowSHint: How much recent discharge history the time-to-reserve estimate uses. 5 to 300 seconds.
battery.reservePercentHint: The charge the time-to-reserve estimate counts down to. 5 to 50 percent.

addNode.noAccountRequired: 계정이 필요하지 않습니다. 완전히 오프라인으로 작동합니다.
addNode.installAgentDescription: SBC에서 이것을 실행한 다음 위에 호스트 이름을 붙여넣으세요.
addNode.signInDescription: 선택 사항입니다. LAN 외부에서 페어링된 노드에 접근할 수 있게 해줍니다.

addNode.probeFailedError: 해당 주소에 연결할 수 없습니다. 에이전트가 실행 중이고 동일한 네트워크에 있는지 확인하세요.
addNode.alreadyPairedMessage: 이 에이전트는 이미 페어링되어 있습니다. 소유권을 가져오려면 로컬에서 페어링하세요. 불가능한 경우 에이전트가 명확한 오류로 응답합니다.
addNode.alreadyPairedToOtherBrowser: 이 에이전트는 이미 다른 브라우저에 페어링되어 있습니다. 에이전트의 설정 페이지에서 페어링을 해제한 후 다시 시도하세요.
addNode.mixedContentError: 이 Mission Control은 HTTPS로 제공됩니다. 브라우저는 HTTPS 페이지에서 일반 HTTP 프로브를 차단합니다. LAN 에이전트를 페어링하려면 Mission Control을 http://로 로드하거나 localhost 빌드를 사용하세요.

addNode.pairHostedRemotelyError: This Mission Control is hosted off your network, so its server cannot reach {host} — the node itself is probably fine. Open a Mission Control on the same network and pair from there: the desktop app, or a local build. If the node really is remote, enable cloud relay on it and pair with its 6-character code.
addNode.pairKeyRejectedError: {host} answered and refused this browser's key — the node is already claimed by a different browser. Run `ados unpair` on the node, or open {settingsUrl} to release it, then press Pair again.
addNode.pairPinRequiredError: {host} answered but will not pair until its dashboard PIN is set. Open {settingsUrl} on this network to set the PIN, then press Pair again.
addNode.pairRouteMissingError: {host} answered but has no pairing endpoint — it is running an older agent, or it is not an ADOS node. Run `ados update` on it, then press Pair again.
addNode.pairTimedOutError: {host} answered but did not finish pairing in time. Press Pair again; if it keeps timing out, check the link with `ados diag link` on the node.
addNode.pairAgentNotReadyError: {host} answered but its pairing service is still starting. Wait a few seconds, then press Pair again.
addNode.pairAgentFaultError: {host} could not save the pairing: {detail}. Check its disk space and service health with `ados status` on the node, then press Pair again.
addNode.pairRefusedError: {host} answered and refused the pairing request. Run `ados status` on the node to check its pairing state, then press Pair again.
addNode.unpairFailedError: Couldn't release {host} from this browser. Run `ados unpair` on the node to release it, then remove it here.
addNode.codeRateLimitedError: Too many pair-code attempts from this browser. Try again in {seconds} s.
addNode.pairedWaitingRelay: Paired. Waiting for the node to report over the cloud relay.
addNode.pairNameUnresolvedError: Mission Control's server could not resolve {host} to an address on your network, so nothing was contacted. Check the name, or try the node's IP address instead.
addNode.pairBadAddressError: {host} is not an address Mission Control can pair with. Use the node's name or IP address on its own, without a path or a different port.
addNode.pairNotAnAgentError: Something at {host} answered, but not the way an ADOS agent does. Check that the address points at the node and that its agent is running.
addNode.pairProxyRefusedError: Mission Control's server would not contact {host} for this page, so the node was never asked. Open Mission Control from this computer or from an address on the node's network, or use the desktop app.

limited.title: Cloud relay connection
limited.network: Network configuration writes through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Connect to the agent's setup page from a device on the same network to change WiFi, Ethernet, modem, or uplink priority.
limited.display: LCD calibration and remote page control write through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Read-only status is in the Overview card.
limited.physicalUi: OLED brightness, screen cycle, and Bluetooth pairing route through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Connect on LAN to make changes.
limited.peripherals: Peripheral rescan and per-peripheral actions route through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. The list below comes from the cloud heartbeat and is read-only.
limited.mesh: batman-adv mesh topology (neighbours, routes, gateways) is local to the ground station and never relayed through the cloud. Connect on LAN to inspect mesh health.
limited.distributedRx: Distributed receive fragment counters and pairing controls are local to the ground station and never relayed through the cloud. Connect on LAN for the live view.
limited.radio: Radio link stats and TX power route through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change its radio.
limited.gnss: The GNSS lane and RTK base are read and set through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change them.
limited.lora: The LoRa lane, its duty governor and region are read and set through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change them.
limited.sensors: Rig sensors, the session clock and capture storage are read straight from the node. Open this node on its local network to see them.

videoLatencyBreakdown.timeFromCameraCaptureOn: 드론의 카메라 캡처부터 화면에 프레임이 표시될 때까지의 시간입니다. H.264 비트스트림의 SEI 타임스탬프 + WebRTC presentationTime + 드론↔브라우저 시계 오프셋 추정치를 사용합니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.droneSideStampToReadback: 드론 측 스탬프-재수신: 인코더가 프레임을 출력한 시점(인코딩 후 SEI 타임스탬프가 삽입되는 지점)부터 해당 프레임을 드론 자체 RTSP 피드에서 다시 읽어 들이기까지의 시간입니다. 송출 먹스, RTSP 송출 및 드론 측 버퍼링을 포함합니다. 카메라 캡처, 인코딩, 무선 링크, 지상 수신 및 브라우저는 제외되므로 glass-to-glass 수치가 아닙니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.numberOfSEISamplesRead: 최근 1초 동안 드론의 로컬 탭이 읽은 SEI 샘플 수입니다. SEI가 정상이면 인코딩 프레임 속도와 거의 같습니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.webrtcICECandidatePairCurrentRoundTripTi: WebRTC ICE 후보 쌍의 currentRoundTripTime입니다. Chrome의 chrome://webrtc-internals에 표시되는 값과 같습니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.inboundRtpJitterVarianceIn: inbound-rtp.jitter. 패킷 도착 시간의 편차로, 값이 높으면 네트워크가 프레임을 불규칙한 간격으로 전달하고 있음을 의미합니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.chromeSDecoderJitterBuffer: Chrome 디코더 지터 버퍼: 각 프레임이 도착 후 디코딩되기까지 대기하는 시간입니다. 네트워크 지터가 크면 늘어나고 링크가 원활하면 줄어듭니다.
videoLatencyBreakdown.cumulativeRTPPacketsTheReceiver: 수신기가 손실로 감지한 누적 RTP 패킷 수입니다. 값이 계속 증가하면 링크 품질 또는 FEC 여유가 부족하다는 뜻입니다.

latency-breakdown-parts.encodePlusNetworkFromRVFC: 인코딩과 네트워크 구간으로, rVFC captureTime부터 receiveTime까지입니다. 원격 소스의 captureTime은 RTCP 송신자 보고와 클럭 동기화를 바탕으로 사용자 에이전트가 추정한 값이므로 실제 값이긴 하지만 정확도는 동기화 수준에 좌우되며, 세션 첫 1초 동안은 사용할 수 없습니다. 하드웨어 인코딩 송출기를 사용하는 정상 LAN의 참고값: 종단 간 약 180 ms P50 / 240 ms P95. 이는 참고값일 뿐 이 링크의 측정값이 아닙니다.

latency-breakdown-parts.rvfcProcessingDurationTheSummedDecode: rVFC processingDuration: 디코더가 보고한 프레임의 총 디코딩 시간입니다.

latency-breakdown-parts.theVSyncTaxFrom: presentationTime부터 expectedDisplayTime까지의 v-sync 지연입니다. expectedDisplayTime은 프레임이 언제 보일지에 대한 사용자 에이전트의 예측값이며, 실제로 표시되었다는 보고가 아닙니다.

latency-breakdown-parts.whatTheControlLoopCurrently: 제어 루프가 현재 수신기의 지터 버퍼에 요청하는 값으로, 측정된 프리즈, RTP 지터 및 손실을 바탕으로 최소 2초 유지 시간을 두고 선택됩니다. 측정 근거 없이 하드코딩되었던 50 ms를 대체합니다. 0은 루프가 버퍼를 추가할 이유를 찾지 못했거나, 이 브라우저가 수신기 설정을 모두 지원하지 않음을 뜻합니다. 프레임이 수신되고 있고 위의 버퍼+합성 구간 값이 상당하다면 이는 브라우저 자체의 버퍼 깊이이며 여기서 설정한 값이 아닙니다.

calibration.compassCalibrationDesc: 완료될 때까지 기체를 모든 방향으로 천천히 회전시키세요.
calibration.compassTip1: 금속 물체, 차량, 건물에서 최소 3m 이상 떨어지세요
calibration.compassTip2: 근처의 자성 악세서리(폰 거치대, 금속 도구)를 제거하세요
calibration.compassTip3: 가능하면 GPS 수신을 확보하세요 (나침반 방향 검증에 도움됩니다)
calibration.compassTip4: 기체를 단단히 잡고 모든 축으로 회전시키세요
calibration.compassOrientationChangedDesc: 캘리브레이션에서 이전 설정과 다른 나침반 방향이 감지되었습니다. 재부팅 후 파라미터에서 장착 방향을 확인하세요.
calibration.bfAccelDone: Betaflight sampled the accelerometer and saved the trims. If the quad moved during calibration, run it again.
calibration.inavAccelDesc: iNav calibrates the accelerometer from six orientations. Start with the vehicle level (top up), then capture upside down and each of the four sides in any order. Hold each orientation still, within about 30 degrees, and press Capture.
calibration.inavAccelCalibrated: The accelerometer is calibrated. Capturing level (top up) starts a new calibration.
calibration.inavAccelNotCaptured: No new orientation was captured. Hold the vehicle still in an orientation that is not captured yet; to recalibrate a calibrated board, start from level (top up).
calibration.inavAccelComplete: All six orientations captured. iNav computed the calibration and saved it.
calibration.inavAccelRejected: iNav rejected the six-orientation fit and cleared the samples. Start again from level (top up).
calibration.inavCompassDesc: Starts iNav's compass calibration. Rotate the vehicle through every orientation until the countdown ends; iNav stores the new offsets when its calibration time (mag_calibration_time) runs out.
calibration.inavCompassRunning: Rotate the vehicle through every orientation: {seconds} s left
calibration.inavCompassTimeUnknown: Could not read mag_calibration_time; timing the default {seconds} s.
calibration.inavCompassUpdated: Compass offsets changed from {before} to {after}; iNav saved them.
calibration.inavCompassUnchanged: Compass offsets did not change {after}. Run it again, rotating through every orientation.
calibration.inavLevelNote: iNav has no level calibration. If the horizon is tilted after accelerometer calibration, correct it with board alignment (align_board_roll and align_board_pitch).
calibration.inavGyroNote: iNav calibrates the gyro at every boot; keep the vehicle still while it powers up.

mcp.title: Control your fleet from your AI assistant
mcp.subtitle: ADOS MCP lets Claude Code and other AI clients read and operate your drones through a scoped, audited, revocable connection you run on your own machine.
mcp.readBody: Live status, telemetry, health, and configuration, with the meaning of every field.
mcp.operateBody: Restart services, manage extensions, and adjust configuration on the node.
mcp.safeBody: A scope on every connection, a confirmation on sensitive actions, and an audit on every call.
mcp.connectBody: Run the server on your own machine and point it at Mission Control, then paste the machine credential you generate here:
mcp.credentialNote: The credential is scoped and revocable, and stored only as a hash. Revoke it any time to cut a server off instantly.
mcp.signInToGenerate: Sign in to Mission Control to generate a credential.
mcp.consoleSubtitle: Machine credentials that let AI clients reach your fleet. Each is scoped and revocable.
mcp.revokeConfirmBody: Any AI client using "{label}" will lose access immediately. This cannot be undone.

read.label: Read only
read.body: Status, telemetry, and parameters. No changes to the fleet.

operate.label: Operate
operate.body: Everything in read, plus services, extensions, config, and tuning. No flight.

full.label: Full control
full.body: Everything, including flight actions. Each flight command still needs a confirmation.

reveal.warning: You will not be able to see this credential again. If you lose it, revoke it and generate a new one.

wizard.title: Set up ADOS MCP
wizard.landingBody: The guided setup gets you connected in a few steps. First, get the server onto your machine:

mint.body: Name this credential and choose what it may do. You'll see the secret once, on the next step.

prereq.title: Before you start
prereq.body: You'll need these on your own machine:
prereq.client: An MCP client — Claude Code, Cursor, or Claude Desktop
prereq.docker: Docker (Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS, Docker Engine on Linux)

get.title: Get the server
get.body: Clone the ADOS MCP repo and build it. The setup script installs, builds, and prints your exact connect command:
get.note: The script prints the command with your local path filled in — you'll paste your credential into it in the last step.
get.dockerBody: Create the folder the server keeps its audit trail in, and pull the image:
get.dockerNote: The image runs as user id 1000. On Linux, if your user id differs, add --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" after docker run.

add.title: Add it to your client
add.body: Run this in your terminal. Your credential is already filled in, and it rides in the client's environment, not your shell:
add.pathNote: Replace <path-to>/ADOS-MCP with the path the setup script printed.
add.jsonAlt: Prefer a project's .mcp.json? Use this instead.
add.warning: This is the only time your credential is shown. Copy the command now — if you lose it, revoke the credential and set up again.
add.localBody: Run this in your terminal. It points the server at your drone over the LAN; the drone's pairing key rides in the client's environment, not your shell:
add.keyNote: The key is this drone's pairing key, stored on this machine when you paired it. To cut a client off, unpair the drone.
add.fleetBody: You picked several drones. Download the fleet file, save it to the path below, then run this — the server reaches your whole LAN fleet, no cloud:
add.savePath: Save it to {path}, then restrict it (chmod 600) — it holds your drones' pairing keys.
add.allBody: Run this one command. Every drone's address and key rides inside it — there is no file to save:
add.fileAlt: Prefer a file? (very large fleets / a saved setup)
add.fileBody: Download the fleet file, save it to the path below, then use this command instead:
add.jsonSecretNote: This .mcp.json reads {name} from your environment, so the file holds no secret and is safe to commit. Set it in your shell with the line below, and keep that value out of shared source: it holds drone pairing keys.
add.dockerNote: The container mounts ~/.ados/mcp so the audit trail persists and this tab's live activity works. Run it in PowerShell or a POSIX shell so $HOME expands; in Git Bash, put MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 in front of the command or Git Bash rewrites the mount path.
add.dockerDiscoverNote: Auto-adopt finds drones over mDNS, which a container on Docker's default network cannot see. On Linux add --network host after docker run; elsewhere use From source for auto-adopt.

verify.body: Once you've added it, run the command (or the check below) — we'll confirm the moment your server authenticates with this credential:
verify.waiting: Waiting for your server to connect…
verify.connected: Connected! Your server authenticated with this credential.
verify.localBody: Once you have added it, run the command below to confirm. We also check the drone directly from here:
verify.fleetBody: Run the command below, or check your drones directly from here:

pick.title: Pick your drones
pick.body: Choose the drones you have already paired on your LAN. Each connection uses that drone's own pairing key, so there is no sign-in and nothing routes through the cloud.
pick.emptyBody: Pair a drone from the Dashboard's Add-a-Node card first, then reopen this setup. Your paired drones appear here automatically.
pick.allBody: The server controls every drone you have paired — one command, no file, no picking.
pick.autoAdopt: Also auto-adopt new drones on my LAN
pick.autoAdoptNote: The server browses your network and pairs itself to any new UNPAIRED drone it finds. Off unless you turn it on.

local.title: Connect a drone on your LAN
local.body: The default path: run the server on your machine and reach a drone directly over your network. No sign-in, no cloud.

cloud.title: Manage from anywhere
cloud.body: Optionally reach your fleet remotely through Mission Control's cloud relay, for when you are off the drone's network. This is the only path that needs a sign-in.

watch.subtitle: Live tool calls
watch.followHint: Auto-navigate to each surface the MCP changes
watch.waitingHint: Run a tool from your AI client and it appears here, live.

mcp.watchBody: Keep Mission Control open and see every action the MCP takes as it happens. The view jumps to the surface being changed and highlights it in real time, so operating a drone through an AI feels like watching a model assemble itself.
mcp.watchPointSee: Every tool call, live — the effect in plain language, not a black box.
mcp.watchPointLocal: Local-first: control and the activity feed both stay on your machine.
mcp.watchPointAudit: Timestamped and recorded — the live feed doubles as your audit trail.

osdScreenPreview.dragElementsToRepositionClick: 요소를 드래그하여 위치를 변경하세요. 사이드바에서 요소를 클릭하면 표시 여부가 전환됩니다.
